philosophical_usage: Hegelian negation is determinate — it preserves the content of what it negates and produces a positive result, unlike abstract negation which simply annihilates
Sublation (Aufhebung) is the triply-valent operation of cancelling, preserving, and elevating — the central engine of Hegelian dialectics
Marx's alienation describes the structural separation of the worker from product, process, species-being, and fellow humans under capitalist production
Heidegger reserves existence (Existenz) for Dasein alone — only Dasein exists in the sense of standing out into its possibilities; other entities merely occur (are present-at-hand)
For Kant, appearance (Erscheinung) is the object of empirical intuition — not mere illusion but the legitimate domain of knowledge, contrasted with the unknowable thing-in-itself
Lacanian desire is metonymic — always sliding along the signifying chain, constitutively unsatisfiable because its true object (objet a) is a structural void, not an attainable thing

Nietzsche's will to power is not domination over others but the internal principle of self-overcoming; Foucault's power is productive and relational, circulating through capillary networks rather than possessed by a sovereign

Derrida's differance (with an a) is the originary movement of differing-and-deferring that precedes and constitutes all identity; Deleuze's difference-in-itself is prior to identity and representation

Heidegger recasts truth as aletheia (unconcealment) — not correspondence between proposition and fact but the event of Being's self-disclosure; for Hegel, truth is the whole, the self-movement of the concept

Kantian freedom is rational self-legislation (autonomy); Hegelian freedom is the insight into necessity; Marxist freedom is the overcoming of material constraints; Sartrean freedom is the inescapable burden of radical choice
In Hegel's Phenomenology, consciousness is the shape of spirit that takes its object as external and opposed; self-consciousness emerges when the object is recognized as consciousness itself
Hegel's decisive move is to show that substance must be grasped equally as subject — the self-moving negativity that develops through its own contradictions rather than resting as inert substrate
Hegelian identity is always identity-in-difference — pure abstract identity (A=A) is empty tautology; concrete identity contains and sublates its difference within itself

Lukacs elevates totality to the central category of Marxist method — only from the standpoint of totality can individual facts be understood; Adorno counters that the whole is the false (das Ganze ist das Unwahre)
The Lacanian subject is the barred subject ($) — constituted by a fundamental lack and split by its entry into language; the Hegelian subject is substance's self-relation through negativity

Kierkegaard's repetition is forward-looking recollection — gaining again what was already possessed; Nietzsche's eternal return tests whether one can affirm each moment's identical recurrence; Deleuze's repetition is the production of difference
Heidegger's Nothing (das Nichts) is not mere logical negation but the ground of anxiety that reveals Being as such; Hegel's pure Being, completely indeterminate, passes immediately into pure Nothing

Hegelian mediation (Vermittlung) is the self-relating negativity through which immediacy is negated and preserved; there is no unmediated immediacy — even the most immediate datum is always already mediated
Marx grounds history in the mode of production — the unity of forces and relations of production; production is not merely economic but constitutes the social being that determines consciousness

Heidegger's anxiety (Angst) has no definite object — it reveals the Nothing and thereby discloses Dasein's being-toward-death; Kierkegaard's anxiety is the dizziness of freedom confronting possibility
Hegel's Anerkennung is the mutual constitution of self-consciousness through the struggle for recognition — the lord-bondsman dialectic shows that genuine recognition requires risking life

Saussure splits the sign into signifier and signified in an arbitrary relation; Derrida shows that the signified is always already another signifier — there is no transcendental signified anchoring the play of signs

Hegel's history is the progress of the consciousness of freedom; Marx inverts this — history is the succession of modes of production driven by class struggle; Foucault replaces continuous history with genealogy of discontinuous epistemes

Kant distinguishes understanding (Verstand, which legislates for phenomena) from reason (Vernunft, which seeks the unconditioned); Hegel reunifies them — reason is the self-articulation of the absolute
Merleau-Ponty's lived body (corps propre) is neither mere object nor pure subject but the pre-reflective ground of perception; Foucault's body is the primary site of disciplinary power's inscription

Kant's moral law is the categorical imperative legislated by pure practical reason; Lacan's symbolic law is the Name-of-the-Father instituting prohibition and desire; Marx's law of value governs commodity exchange

Aristotelian form (morphe/eidos) is the actuality that determines matter; Kantian form is the a priori structure that organizes sensory manifold; Hegelian form is inseparable from content — the content generates its own form

Hegel's nature is the Idea in its otherness — spirit externalized; Schelling's nature is unconscious spirit striving toward consciousness; Marx's nature is the inorganic body of humanity transformed through labor
Heidegger: language is the house of Being, not a tool of communication; Wittgenstein: the limits of my language mean the limits of my world; Lacan: the unconscious is structured like a language

Heidegger's being-toward-death is Dasein's ownmost, non-relational, not-to-be-outstripped possibility that individualizes and reveals authentic temporality; Epicurus dissolves death by arguing it is nothing to us

Kant: time is the pure form of inner sense, not an objective property; Heidegger: temporality (Zeitlichkeit) is the meaning of Dasein's being — ecstatic unity of past (having-been), present, and future

Heidegger's Ereignis is the event of appropriation in which Being and Dasein are mutually constituted; Badiou's event is the undecidable rupture that founds a new truth-procedure, requiring a subject's fidelity

Levinas: the Other (Autrui) is the face that commands 'thou shalt not kill' — ethics as first philosophy; Lacan: the big Other is the symbolic order; Hegel: the other is the moment of self-consciousness's doubling

Heidegger's Abgrund (abyss/unground) reveals that the ultimate ground of beings is groundlessness; Hegel's ground (Grund) is the unity of identity and difference in the logic of essence; Leibniz's principle of sufficient reason demands a ground for every fact

Heidegger: the essence (Wesen) of Dasein lies in its existence — its what is its how; Sartre inverts the tradition: existence precedes essence; Marx: the human essence is the ensemble of social relations, not an abstraction inherent in each individual

Marx distinguishes abstract labor (homogeneous expenditure of human energy creating value) from concrete labor (specific useful activity creating use-values); Hegel's bondsman gains self-consciousness through the discipline of labor on the thing

For Hegel, the limit (Grenze) is both the boundary of the finite and its point of contact with the infinite — to posit a limit is already to have gone beyond it; Kant's limits of reason define the domain of legitimate knowledge

Marx's ideology is the inverted consciousness produced by inverted social relations; Althusser's ideology interpellates individuals as subjects through ideological state apparatuses; Zizek adds that ideology functions even when we know it is false (cynical reason)

Schopenhauer's Will is the blind, irrational thing-in-itself driving all phenomena; Nietzsche transforms it into will to power as self-overcoming; Kant's good will is the only thing good without qualification
